goant can now host a program that does not fit inside it.

A Runtime was a closed world: every job the loop ran was work JavaScript had
already made, so an embedder had no way to answer a question later, from another
goroutine, at a real time. That is what this release changes.

- `WithModuleResolver` — the host says where a bare specifier lives, and may
  supply the source for a module that is not on disk at all
- `NewPromise`, `Post`, `HostRef` / `HostUnref`, `RunLoop(ctx)` — a promise made
  in Go and settled from another goroutine, with the loop staying alive while an
  answer is outstanding
- `WithRealTimers` and `UnrefTimer` / `RefTimer` — a clock that actually elapses,
  and Node's `timer.unref()` for a watchdog that must not be the reason a program
  is still running
- `import.meta.url` and `structuredClone`

Four engine bugs that only a large real program finds, all fixed: a loop body's
`let` and `const` were not per-iteration, so every closure made in a loop shared
one slot; `window` and `globalThis` could not be used as binding names; a regex
built at run time lost its lone surrogates; and an engine-thrown TypeError
carried no stack, so "value is not a function" named neither a file nor a frame.

The proof is [go-deepseek](https://github.com/robomotionio/go-deepseek), which
runs the DeepSeek Harness — 64 modules of somebody else's JavaScript, no Node.js
anywhere — on this engine.

Binaries below are the `goant` CLI for six platforms. It runs the JIT by
default; `goant -jit=false` turns it off.

To embed the package: `go get github.com/robomotionio/goant` (the JIT is
opt-in there, via `WithJIT(true)`).
